Stand-ins and the Army of 64

Bots that fill a dungeon's empty seats, and a test army made of them

Bodies and Mindsbuilt; waiting for the compile

A stand-in is a bot character made to fill a seat a player's own buddies can't: a missing tank or healer in a dungeon, or the doubled places in a battleground. The owner, 2026-10-29, on the test army: "Yeah we should treat them like as if we had 64 buddy-bots."

Dealt at random

The army of 64 (.buddy army 64) is made of stand-ins, each of the game master's side and level. The owner, 2026-10-29: "fully random talent spec profile distribution." So each one gets a random race and class of its side, then one of the ten talent shapes a buddy can have, every shape equally likely, and its role is whatever that shape is.

What fully random makes

Over every Horde race, class and shape, drawn evenly, the roles come out (from the stand-ins' test, scripts/test-buddy-stand-ins):

RoleDrawsShare
damage25984%
tank186%
healer3311%

So a random army of 64 holds about 4 tanks and 7 healers.

A stand-in's life

  1. Made when a seat needs it, dressed and gemmed for its level.
  2. In play in the dungeon or battleground, its talent plan steering its gear and gems like a buddy's.
  3. Kept afterwards, out of the world, never deleted.
  4. Met again by chance, and raised one level a match (the owner: "one level.").

Met by chance

The owner, 2026-10-29: "there shouldn't be a set path, it should just be... if you happen to see them, they'll level with you. it's random." When a player needs a stand-in, one of the kept ones that fits (the same race, class and role, at or below the level needed) is drawn at random and raised to the level it is needed at. Its level never goes down.

Filling the seats

In a dungeon, a player's own buddies sit first (the dungeon draw picks them without replacement). A seat no buddy can fill, a tank or healer missing, is filled by a stand-in.
